title: Dexmedetomidine may alleviate severe acute pancreatitis-associated lung injury by targeting the AIM2 inflammasome in endothelial cells.
authors: Zhou, Jing; Ge, Peng; Cui, Jinhua; Xuan, Guocheng; Ma, Chi; Yao, Jiaqi; Wen, Qingping
one_liner_zh: 该文研究右美托咪定通过靶向AIM2炎症小体减轻重症急性胰腺炎相关肺损伤，属于药物机制与炎症信号通路研究，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is often associated with life-threatening acute lung injury (ALI), with its pathogenesis being intricately connected to dysregulated inflammatory responses. There is a deficiency of particular treatment options. Dexmedetomidine (DEX), a highly selective alpha2-adrenergic receptor (alpha2-AR) agonist, demonstrates not only sedative effects but also possesses anti-inflammatory and organ-protective properties. However, the mechanisms through which DEX exerts its effects in SAP and related pulmonary disorders remain uncertain. METHODS: A rat SAP model was established via retrograde injection of 5% sodium taurocholate into the biliopancreatic ducts, with DEX intervention and positive control groups included. The effects of DEX on pathological damage to pancreatic and lung tissues, serum inflammatory factors, and pulmonary edema were evaluated in vivo. In vitro, lipopolysaccharide (LPS) stimulation of human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) was used to model an inflammatory environment. Transcriptome sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing data analysis, protein-protein interaction network construction, molecular docking, and molecular biology techniques were employed to investigate the action targets of DEX and its regulatory effects on the absent in melanoma 2 (AIM2) inflammasome signaling pathway. RESULTS: DEX therapy attenuated the pathological injury to pancreatic and pulmonary tissues in SAP rats, decreased serum concentrations of amylase, interleukin-1 beta, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha, and suppressed pulmonary edema. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that DEX could partially reverse the disorder in lung tissue gene expression profiles induced by SAP and identified the "DEX target gene set". Bioinformatics analysis identified AIM2 as the core target, and molecular docking indicated that DEX could bind to AIM2 effectively. Single-cell RNA sequencing analysis revealed that the target gene set was specifically highly expressed in endothelial cells. DEX inhibited the activation of AIM2 and Caspase-11, as well as the phosphorylation of the nuclear factor kappa-B signaling pathway in lung tissue and endothelial cells. It also decreased the expression of vascular cell adhesion protein-1 and matrix metalloproteinase-9 in lung tissue. In addition, AIM2 knocdown blocked LPS-induced apoptosis in HUVECs, and DEX showed no further inhibitory effect. CONCLUSION: This study identifies a novel mechanism in which DEX may alleviate pyroptosis of endothelial cells by targeting and inhibiting AIM2 inflammasome activation, thereby improving SAP-ALI.
abstract_zh: 背景：重症急性胰腺炎（SAP）常伴随危及生命的急性肺损伤（ALI），其发病机制与炎症反应失调密切相关。目前缺乏特定的治疗选择。右美托咪定（DEX），一种高选择性α2-肾上腺素能受体（alpha2-AR）激动剂，不仅具有镇静作用，还具备抗炎和器官保护特性。然而，DEX在SAP及相关肺部疾病中发挥作用的机制仍不明确。方法：通过向胆胰管逆行注射5%牛磺胆酸钠建立大鼠SAP模型，并设置DEX干预组和阳性对照组。在体内评估DEX对胰腺和肺组织病理损伤、血清炎症因子及肺水肿的影响。在体外，使用脂多糖（LPS）刺激人脐静脉内皮细胞（HUVECs）以模拟炎症环境。采用转录组测序、单细胞RNA测序数据分析、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用网络构建、分子对接和分子生物学技术，研究DEX的作用靶点及其对黑色素瘤缺失因子2（AIM2）炎症小体信号通路的调控作用。结果：DEX治疗减轻了SAP大鼠胰腺和肺组织的病理损伤，降低了血清中淀粉酶、白细胞介素-1β和肿瘤坏死因子-α的浓度，并抑制了肺水肿。转录组分析显示，DEX可部分逆转SAP诱导的肺组织基因表达谱紊乱，并识别出“DEX靶基因集”。生物信息学分析确定AIM2为核心靶点，分子对接表明DEX能有效结合AIM2。单细胞RNA测序分析显示，靶基因集在内皮细胞中特异性高表达。DEX抑制了肺组织和内皮细胞中AIM2和Caspase-11的激活，以及核因子kappa-B信号通路的磷酸化。它还降低了肺组织中血管细胞黏附蛋白-1和基质金属蛋白酶-9的表达。此外，AIM2敲低阻断了LPS诱导的HUVECs凋亡，而DEX未表现出进一步的抑制作用。结论：本研究揭示了一种新机制，即DEX可能通过靶向并抑制AIM2炎症小体激活来减轻内皮细胞焦亡，从而改善SAP-ALI。
